Marcus Delgado (mdelgado) confirmed normal access restored from WORKSTATION-DELL-MD at 05:04 UTC.

Reset MFA enrollment for users whose existing factor state was stale or inconsistent â€” specifically ranguyen and dkowalski â€” so they could re-register a valid active Okta Verify factor. Instructed affected users (mbell and pdeshmukh) to resync authenticator application time via Settings > Time Correction in the Okta Verify app, and correct device clock settings on endpoints showing more than five minutes of drift. Validated post-change sign-ins through the Okta to Azure AD flow for all four affected users (ranguyen, dkowalski, mbell, pdeshmukh) and monitored authentication logs for 24 hours to confirm prompt loops and SSO rejections stopped across the affected application set (Salesforce, G Suite, Confluence). Confirmed NAC policy 'CorpWiFi-FullAccess' was correctly applied post-renewal for users mchen, rpatel, and others. Had impacted users forget the Corporate SSID (CorpNet-Secure) and reconnect; for devices that continued to fail â€” including WORKSTATION-LAPTOP-MC (mchen), and endpoints for rpatel and jmartinez â€” removed the stale wireless profile and re-enrolled the device into the corporate Wi-Fi configuration via the MDM portal. Monitored post-change authentication attempts across floors 3 and 4 in Portland and confirmed successful NAC authorization and restored network access across the affected user population. Final confirmation received from Maria Chen (EMP-40821) and Raj Patel at 05:45 UTC. No further NAC denials observed in the subsequent 2-hour monitoring window.

retrieved_fault: Internal hostname fails to resolve. Users and monitoring in the Newark region were trying to reach the Internal App Service by the hostname internal-app.service.local, but since about 06:15 UTC on 2026-01-15 the name intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or timed out from the internal DNS resolver cluster (resolver-01.dns.corp.internal / resolver-02.dns.corp.internal). This prevented the Internal Portal and dependent application calls from reaching the service endpoint by name and caused multi-tier application errors. Initially reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com, ext. 4417) from the DevOps team, and corroborated by alerts from Network Monitoring dashboards. Affected users include members of the platform engineering and QA groups working from the Newark office.
retrieved_root_cause: Internal DNS resolvers served stale cache data for internal-app.service.local, including an outdated A record pointing to a decommissioned IP, while TTL mismatch between the authoritative zone and resolver cache allowed the incorrect response to persist intermittently across resolver-01 and resolver-02.
retrieved_resolution: Verified the authoritative internal DNS zone entry on ns-auth-01.dns.corp.internal for internal-app.service.local and confirmed the A record was already updated to the current service IP 10.40.2.30; corrected the residual TTL value from 86400 to 300 seconds to match policy. Flushed cached DNS entries on resolver-01.dns.corp.internal and resolver-02.dns.corp.internal using rndc flush to remove the stale record (10.40.1.15) and clear intermittent NXDOMAIN and timeout responses affecting users in the Newark region. Restarted the DNS resolver service (named) on resolver-01.dns.corp.internal where persistent cached data was observed to ensure fresh zone data was served and no in-memory stale entries remained. Validated name resolution from multiple internal clients â€” including Marcus Delgado's workstation WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.22.4.87), the QA jump host at 10.22.6.50, and Network Monitoring probes in Newark and Ashburn â€” and confirmed queries returned the corrected A record (10.40.2.30) consistently. Adjusted the internal TTL policy for service records to 300 seconds on ns-auth-01.dns.corp.internal and aligned resolver caching behavior (max-cache-ttl) on resolver-01 and resolver-02 to reduce the chance of prolonged stale responses. Change documented by Raj Okonkwo (rokonkwo) and reviewed by Priya Nair.

retrieved_fault: UDM communication failing due to certificate issue
retrieved_resolution: There appears to be a security or trust issue between the UDM and other network components. If the UDM does not trust the credentials or certificates from other services (or those services do not trust the UDM) secure communication will fail. This often occurs due to an expired certificate or a certificate mismatch or misconfigured security settings. This results in TLS handshake failures or rejected connections. Verify the certificates and security configurations on the UDM and the peer entities (such as the AMF or AUSF). Ensure that the UDM certificates are valid and not expired and that they are recognized as trusted by the other components. Likewise confirm that the UDM trusts the certificates of its peers. If any certificate is expired or untrusted then install a valid certificate and adjust the trust settings accordingly. Once the security settings are corrected the UDM should be able to communicate securely with other network functions.

retrieved_resolution: A configuration error in the UDM is causing it to behave incorrectly. For example if the UDM is not configured to serve a specific PLMN or if there is a misconfiguration in its interface settings it may fail to respond correctly to certain requests. Such issues would manifest as UDM errors whenever that particular configuration is invoked. Review the configuration files or settings of the UDM. Look for obvious errors like incorrect PLMN IDs network identifiers or interface endpoints that the UDM uses to communicate with other functions. If the UDM is meant to handle multiple PLMNs or network slices ensure those are correctly configured in its settings. After fixing any configuration mistakes restart the UDM if necessary and test the request again to confirm that the UDM responds correctly.

retrieved_fault: Security configuration error between UDM and core network
retrieved_resolution: There appears to be a security or trust issue between the UDM and other network components. If the UDM does not trust the credentials or certificates from other services (or those services do not trust the UDM) secure communication will fail. This often occurs due to an expired certificate or a certificate mismatch or misconfigured security settings. This results in TLS handshake failures or rejected connections. Verify the certificates and security configurations on the UDM and the peer entities (such as the AMF or AUSF). Ensure that the UDM certificates are valid and not expired and that they are recognized as trusted by the other components. Likewise confirm that the UDM trusts the certificates of its peers. If any certificate is expired or untrusted then install a valid certificate and adjust the trust settings accordingly. Once the security settings are corrected the UDM should be able to communicate securely with other network functions.

This resulted in a localized outage: UEs on the affected gNodeBs lost data service and could not register whereas other UEs continued normally.

To avoid such issues; the AMF was configured with link redundancy so that if one interface fails traffic automatically shifts to another without interruption.

retrieved_fault: AMF user capacity exceeded and new devices cannot register
retrieved_resolution: The AMF may have reached its capacity limits. If the AMF has a maximum number of subscribers or sessions it can handle (due to hardware limits or license restrictions) exceeding that limit will prevent new devices from registering. In this scenario the AMF is essentially out of resources for additional connections. To fix this check the AMF resource utilization and licensing status. If a limit has been reached you may need to increase the capacity by adding more resources or obtain a higher-capacity license. Additionally ensure that stale sessions or inactive users are cleared from the AMF so they do not consume capacity unnecessarily.

retrieved_fault: UPF not handling large packets properly
retrieved_resolution: The UPF is likely dropping packets due to an MTU or fragmentation issue. Packets larger than the supported MTU might be discarded by the UPF if fragmentation is not handled properly. This can result in connectivity problems especially for large data transfers. Check the MTU settings on the UPF and along the path to the data network. Ensure that MTU values are consistent or that the UPF is configured to fragment packets when necessary. If there is an MTU mismatch adjust the MTU on the UPF or other network devices to a uniform value. Test with large packet sizes after aligning the MTU settings to confirm that the UPF no longer drops packets due to fragmentation issues.

retrieved_fault: SMF missing subscriber data from UDM
retrieved_resolution: The SMF might not have the necessary subscriber data for the session. The SMF may deny the session if it cannot retrieve the subscriber profile (such as allowed services or slice info) from the UDM. This could happen due to missing information in the subscriber profile or a communication error with the UDM. Check that the subscriber profile in the UDM contains all required information (for example allowed DNNs and QoS parameters). Verify that the SMF can query the UDM (or UDR) and is receiving the necessary data. If the subscriber data is incomplete update the profile in the UDM. Restoring proper subscriber information and connectivity should enable the SMF to set up the session.

retrieved_fault: UDM lacks subscriber information
retrieved_resolution: The UDM does not have the required subscriber data available. This can occur if the subscriber is not provisioned in the UDM or if their profile information is incomplete. This means that requests for that subscriber data (such as authentication or service profile) are failing. Verify that the subscriber in question is properly provisioned in the UDM database. Check that all essential details (IMSI and subscription plan and allowed services) are present in the profile. If the profile is missing then create or update the subscriber record with the correct information. Once the subscriber data is in place the UDM will be able to supply the needed information to other network functions.

retrieved_fault: AMF to SMF communication error during session setup
retrieved_resolution: The AMF is having trouble assigning or communicating with an SMF for session management. This could happen if the AMF cannot find a suitable SMF for the requested session perhaps due to a network slice configuration issue or missing DNN information. It might also indicate that the AMF-SMF interface is misconfigured or the SMF is not registered properly in the core network. To resolve this verify that the NSSF is providing the correct slice and that an SMF is available for that slice. Check that the SMF is properly registered and discoverable (for example via the NRF) and that the AMF has the correct configuration to reach it. Correcting any configuration mismatches or registering the SMF properly should allow the AMF to forward session requests to the SMF.

retrieved_fault: Unconfigured DNN requested causing SMF to reject session
retrieved_resolution: The SMF is encountering a Data Network Name (DNN) issue. If the SMF does not recognize the DNN the UE is requesting it will reject the session. This can occur if the DNN is not configured on the SMF or if there is a typo or mismatch in the DNN configuration. Verify that the DNN (equivalent to an APN in 4G terms) requested by the UE is configured on the SMF. If not add the correct DNN configuration or have the UE use an available DNN. The SMF should accept the session once the configuration is updated if the DNN is valid for that subscriber.

retrieved_fault: AMF resource exhaustion limiting new attach attempts
retrieved_resolution: The AMF may have reached its capacity limits. If the AMF has a maximum number of subscribers or sessions it can handle (due to hardware limits or license restrictions) exceeding that limit will prevent new devices from registering. In this scenario the AMF is essentially out of resources for additional connections. To fix this check the AMF resource utilization and licensing status. retrieved_resolution: There seems to be a security configuration issue affecting the AMF connectivity. If the AMF is not connecting due to a certificate mismatch or TLS handshake error it means the secure communication between the AMF and another core component is failing. retrieved_fault: UDM returns missing profile for subscriber
retrieved_resolution: The UDM does not have the required subscriber data available. This can occur if the subscriber is not provisioned in the UDM or if their profile information is incomplete. This means that requests for that subscriber data (such as authentication or service profile) are failing. Verify that the subscriber in question is properly provisioned in the UDM database. Check that all essential details (IMSI and subscription plan and allowed services) are present in the profile. If the profile is missing then create or update the subscriber record with the correct information. Once the subscriber data is in place the UDM will be able to supply the needed information to other network functions.

retrieved_fault: UDM subscription profile missing policy details
retrieved_resolution: There is an inconsistency in subscriber information between the UDM and other components like the NSSF or PCF. This can happen if the UDM lacks updated details that the NSSF or PCF expects such as permitted network slices or policy information for the subscriber. As a result when those components query the UDM they either get incorrect info or none leading to slice selection or policy application failures. Review the subscriber profile in the UDM for completeness regarding new features like network slicing and policy settings. Ensure that the allowed slice list for the subscriber (S-NSSAI information) is present and up to date if slice-based services are being used. Likewise verify that any policy-related data which the PCF might retrieve is correctly stored in the UDM. If discrepancies are found update the UDM records to match the intended configuration so that NSSF and PCF queries return consistent information.

retrieved_fault: UPF not handling large packets properly
retrieved_resolution: The UPF is likely dropping packets due to an MTU or fragmentation issue. Packets larger than the supported MTU might be discarded by the UPF if fragmentation is not handled properly. This can result in connectivity problems especially for large data transfers. Check the MTU settings on the UPF and along the path to the data network. Ensure that MTU values are consistent or that the UPF is configured to fragment packets when necessary. If there is an MTU mismatch adjust the MTU on the UPF or other network devices to a uniform value. Test with large packet sizes after aligning the MTU settings to confirm that the UPF no longer drops packets due to fragmentation issues.

Investigate the UPF logs and any crash dumps for clues about the failure. Check if there are known issues with the current software version and consult the vendor or release notes for any available patches. Restarting the UPF might temporarily restore service but the permanent fix will be to apply an update or patch to eliminate the bug. After applying the fix or workaround monitor the UPF to confirm that it remains stable under normal operations.

Verified conditional forwarder and zone routing configuration between internal resolvers DNS-RES-EAST-01 / DNS-RES-EAST-02 and the authoritative DNS server DNS-AUTH-EAST-01, then added the missing forwarder path on DNS-RES-EAST-02 for the corp.eastnet.local namespace. Flushed DNS cache on impacted internal resolvers DNS-RES-EAST-01 and DNS-RES-EAST-02 (dnscmd /clearcache) and repeated lookups to remove stale answers (10.40.2.17) previously being served from cache. Retested name resolution from multiple resolver paths and client locations â€” including WORKSTATION-PC-MD (10.40.12.88, mdelgado), APPNODE-EAST-04, and APPNODE-EAST-07 â€” using repeated nslookup/dig queries to confirm the same current address was returned consistently for all three affected service hostnames. Enabled follow-up monitoring via Network Monitoring for internal name resolution on the corp.eastnet.local zone so future NXDOMAIN, timeout, or stale-answer patterns can be correlated with affected hostnames and timing if the issue recurs. retrieved_fault: UDM does not list slice requested by UE
retrieved_resolution: There is an inconsistency in subscriber information between the UDM and other components like the NSSF or PCF. This can happen if the UDM lacks updated details that the NSSF or PCF expects such as permitted network slices or policy information for the subscriber. As a result when those components query the UDM they either get incorrect info or none leading to slice selection or policy application failures. Review the subscriber profile in the UDM for completeness regarding new features like network slicing and policy settings. Ensure that the allowed slice list for the subscriber (S-NSSAI information) is present and up to date if slice-based services are being used. Likewise verify that any policy-related data which the PCF might retrieve is correctly stored in the UDM. If discrepancies are found update the UDM records to match the intended configuration so that NSSF and PCF queries return consistent information.

retrieved_resolution: The UPF may be experiencing a hardware-related problem affecting packet forwarding. For instance a faulty network interface card or insufficient memory can cause the UPF to drop packets or perform poorly. Hardware malfunctions often lead to intermittent errors that impact throughput. Examine the system logs on the UPF for any hardware error indications (for example NIC driver errors or memory warnings). If a particular network interface is dropping packets then consider replacing that interface or updating its driver. Ensure that the server running the UPF has adequate CPU and memory resources and that there are no hardware component failures. Replacing or repairing faulty hardware and allocating sufficient resources should allow the UPF to return to normal operation.

retrieved_resolution: SMF should orchestrate PFCP session restoration without immediately reusing F-TEIDs. Configure UPF to suppress error indications for a period after restart. SMF should control restoration load and include restoration indication in PFCP Session Establishment requests. Validate recovery timestamp handling.

retrieved_fault: UPF keeps restarting due to a bug
retrieved_resolution: The UPF is behaving unreliably. This suggests a potential software bug. Symptoms such as the UPF process crashing or restarting indicate an internal error. It could be triggered by a known issue in the software (perhaps due to certain traffic patterns) or a memory leak that eventually causes a failure. Investigate the UPF logs and any crash dumps for clues about the failure. Check if there are known issues with the current software version and if so apply the recommended patches or updates. Restarting the UPF might temporarily restore service but a software update or configuration change is required for a permanent solution. After applying the fix monitor the UPF to ensure it remains stable under load.

retrieved_fault: Expired TLS certificate on Internal Web Service behind Load Balancer. Users in the Arlington office were trying to reach the Internal Web Service (svc-internal.corplabs.internal) over HTTPS through the F5 load balancer (lb-prod-east-01.corplabs.internal), but browsers and internal integrations continued to reject the connection with NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID warnings and TLS trust failures. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (emp ID E-40821) at 08:32 UTC via the #infra-alerts Slack channel. The service remained intermittently inaccessible after a recent renewal effort, with reports indicating the issue was affecting internal clients in us-east-1 during normal application access. Additional reports came from jparker and dtran, who confirmed the same behavior from their workstations WORKSTATION-MC-4082 and WORKSTATION-DT-7761 respectively.
retrieved_root_cause: The F5 load balancer served a certificate bundle containing an expired intermediate certificate even though the endpoint certificate itself had been renewed successfully. Monitoring and deployment evidence were insufficient to confirm when the active LB chain diverged from the intended full bundle.
retrieved_resolution: Rebuild the full certificate bundle with the renewed server certificate (CN=svc-internal.corplabs.internal, serial 0A:3F:7B:22) and the correct current intermediate chain (DigiCert SHA2 Secure Server CA, valid through 2031-11-09) from the issuing CA. Bundle assembled by nwong and verified with openssl verify -CAfile. Explicitly bind the corrected chain bundle (intermediate-digicert-2026.crt) to the F5 virtual server vs-svc-internal-443 via SSL profile ssl-svc-internal and remove the stale intermediate object intermediate-digicert-2024.crt and any legacy chain references from lb-prod-east-01.corplabs.internal. Configuration change approved by Robert Fielding (rfielding). Validate trust from multiple client paths (tested from 10.42.18.97 in Arlington and 10.55.6.203 in Denver) and directly from the F5 configuration (tmsh show sys crypto cert-chain) to confirm no expired intermediate is presented. Maria Chen (mchen) and jparker confirmed HTTPS access restored without warnings from WORKSTATION-MC-4082 and WORKSTATION-DT-7761. Add chain-level monitoring for the LB-served path on lb-prod-east-01 in the cert-monitor dashboard, covering both leaf and intermediate expiry for svc-internal, and require post-deployment evidence capture (automated openssl chain validation) for the active certificate bundle after every renewal job. Monitoring rule created by dtran (E-60215) and assigned to the Arlington infrastructure team.

retrieved_fault: UDM communication failing due to certificate issue
retrieved_resolution: There appears to be a security or trust issue between the UDM and other network components. If the UDM does not trust the credentials or certificates from other services (or those services do not trust the UDM) secure communication will fail. This often occurs due to an expired certificate or a certificate mismatch or misconfigured security settings. This results in TLS handshake failures or rejected connections. Verify the certificates and security configurations on the UDM and the peer entities (such as the AMF or AUSF). Ensure that the UDM certificates are valid and not expired and that they are recognized as trusted by the other components. Likewise confirm that the UDM trusts the certificates of its peers. If any certificate is expired or untrusted then install a valid certificate and adjust the trust settings accordingly. Once the security settings are corrected the UDM should be able to communicate securely with other network functions.

Replaced the deprecated EnforceEncryption_v1 compliance policy reference with EnforceEncryption_v2 so the current BitLocker telemetry mapping is used during evaluation. Change implemented by endpoint admin krobles. Published the updated compliance policy to the Sales Laptops group in the Charlotte office and initiated a policy refresh so devices would pull the corrected assignment and reprocess compliance state. Monitored post-refresh check-in and compliance results until impacted devices (mcastillo, dhines, pnair) updated from noncompliant to compliant and Conditional Access blocks cleared. Confirmed with Maria Castillo at mcastillo@corplabs.com that access to corporate resources was restored.

Packets larger than the supported MTU might be discarded by the UPF if fragmentation is not handled properly. This can result in connectivity problems especially for large data transfers. Check the MTU settings on the UPF and along the path to the data network. Ensure that MTU values are consistent or that the UPF is configured to fragment packets when necessary. If there is an MTU mismatch adjust the MTU on the UPF or other network devices to a uniform value. Test with large packet sizes after aligning the MTU settings to confirm that the UPF no longer drops packets due to fragmentation issues.

retrieved_fault: Print jobs stuck on ps-nyc-print01. Multiple users in the NYC office reported by floor coordinator Maria Chen were trying to print to shared queue HP-Color-01 on print server ps-nyc-print01, but jobs remained held in the queue and reported driver unavailable errors instead of completing. Restarting the Print Spooler temporarily cleared blocked jobs, but new print attempts failed again within minutes. The issue affected office printing for all users in the Manhattan office relying on the shared server-hosted queue until the server driver package was validated and corrected.
retrieved_root_cause: Corrupted printer driver package HP-Color-Driver-v5.2 on ps-nyc-print01 caused checksum mismatch and prevented the queue from binding the correct driver, leaving jobs stuck in Held status.
retrieved_resolution: Removed the corrupted HP-Color-Driver-v5.2 package from print server ps-nyc-print01 using the Print Management console, clearing all cached driver files from the C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\x64 directory. Installed the approved HP-Color-Driver-v5.2 package from the central repository (\\repo-nyc-fs01\PrintDrivers\HP-Color-v5.2) after validating it against the approved SHA256 checksum (9a3f...c7b1). Cleared all 14 stuck jobs from queue HP-Color-01 and restarted the Print Spooler service on ps-nyc-print01 to reload the corrected driver files into memory. Remapped queue HP-Color-01 to the newly installed driver package on ps-nyc-print01 to restore proper driver binding, and confirmed the queue status returned to Ready. Ran validation test prints from workstations of dkumar (WORKSTATION-PC-DK), jpark, and tnguyen through the shared queue and confirmed all jobs processed successfully without recurring driver unavailable errors. Notified floor coordinator Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) that printing was restored.

retrieved_fault: UPF misrouting traffic to data network
retrieved_resolution: The UPF is not forwarding traffic to the external data network correctly. This usually indicates a routing or NAT configuration problem on the UPF. If the UPF lacks a proper route to the data network (internet) or if NAT is configured incorrectly then user traffic will not reach its destination. Verify the routing table and NAT settings on the UPF. Ensure that the UPF has a route to the data network and that any required NAT rules are in place. Check that the NAT function on the UPF is working correctly for user traffic (if the UPF is expected to perform address translation). Fix any missing routes or misconfigurations in NAT so that the UPF can forward traffic to the internet successfully.

Verify the routing table and NAT settings on the UPF. Ensure that the UPF has a route to the data network and that any required NAT rules are in place. Check that the NAT function on the UPF is working correctly for user traffic (if the UPF is expected to perform address translation). Fix any missing routes or misconfigurations in NAT so that the UPF can forward traffic to the internet successfully.

Restarting the Print Spooler service briefly released some jobs, but the queue quickly blocked again with the same driver unavailable error. Remap the impacted department printer queues (\\PDQ-Print01\Sales-Main and \\PDQ-Print01\HR-Floor2-Queue) from the stale v6.7.2 driver version to the corrected approved v6.9.0-hotfix driver package, updating queue-to-driver assignments in Print Management. If any queue still referenced the bad v6.9.0 package, roll back to the last known-good approved driver package (v6.7.2) and revalidate queue-to-driver assignments. Confirmed the BitLocker recovery key (ID 8A3F2B**) escrowed to Azure AD for device LAPTOP-SALES-MR under user mreeves@corplabs.com, and that Intune compliance updated from 'Encryption - Failed' to compliant. Notified Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com) that the device is now fully compliant.

retrieved_fault: UDM database replication error
retrieved_resolution: The UDM is experiencing an internal database error. If the UDM database has connectivity issues or has failed then the UDM cannot query or update subscriber information as needed. This situation causes errors when other network functions attempt to retrieve data like authentication vectors or subscription profiles. Examine the UDM internal logs for database connectivity or error messages. Ensure that the UDM can reach its data store (for instance the UDR or internal database). If there are replication issues or the database service is down then restore connectivity or restart the database service. Once the database is operational and accessible the UDM should resume handling requests properly.

retrieved_fault: Stale data in UDM causing errors
retrieved_resolution: The data in the UDM for some subscribers is outdated or not synchronized with the latest information. The UDM might be working with old subscription details. This can lead to mismatches when other services use updated data. One scenario is that recent changes to a subscriber profile (like a new service or updated credentials) were not applied to the UDM. Ensure that the subscriber profiles in the UDM have the latest information. If there is a separate provisioning system then make sure it has successfully updated the UDM with any recent changes. For example if a user changed plans or got a new SIM verify that the UDM reflects those updates. If it does not then manually synchronize or refresh the UDM data for those subscribers. Keeping the UDM data current will resolve mismatches due to outdated information.
